thesis: A sparse MoE buys total capacity without paying per-token compute. On CPU that is the whole game: capacity per FLOP decides what a domain model can hold, and therefore whether it can run where the work actually happens.
hardware: 2015 iMac, Intel i7-4790K, 32 GB RAM, CPU only, no CUDA, no MPS

deployability.note: A 19.3 M model is 38 MB in fp16 — it fits in a browser tab, a phone, or a raspberry pi. That is not a marketing point: it decides whether a field researcher, a rural clinic, or an offline laptop can run it at all.

measured_on_this_machine.note: retrieval + generation over 5 passages, CPU only, measured through /api/query

confounds_stated: the MoE run used 2 torch threads, the dense run 1 — the throughput comparison is therefore NOT clean and is reported as suggestive, not causal
both runs saw the same 1,638,400 tokens (200 steps), which is ~0.9 % of compute-optimal for either size — an undertrained comparison, valid for architecture ablation, useless for capability
single seed each; different corpus snapshots between the two runs
what_this_does_not_claim: that this model beats a frontier model at open-ended writing — it does not, and the demo shows it
that 0.91 nats transfers to a larger scale — one endpoint, one seed
that CPU inference replaces GPU training — training still wants a GPU; serving does not
